fused-o algebra (od + scale*b*qk*u, pass-2 eliminated) + coalesced stores: CORRECT but ~1.6x SLOWER than v2 — od dual-staging doubled smem traffic in the hot loop; coalesced-store staging round-trip cost > strided-store penalty (writes are fire-and-forget; L2 absorbs stride). v2 remains FlyDSL best.

FLA-structure port (col-tile programs NV=4, register state, 6 barriers vs 16): correctness best-yet; perf ~= v2 (0.48-0.50x). Two bugs caught: L2N group indexing (base+tid -> base+g8), qk not renormalized (needs inv_q*inv_k). Same-wall as v2 => shared bottleneck, not structure.

At B=1 BOTH impls are dispatch-bound (FLA wall 44us = 38 dispatch + 6 kernel). v4wrapper adds another 47-133us Python (reshape/contiguous/alloc per step).

B=128 FLA kernel runs at 5.1TB/s effective state BW (1.6GB fp32 round-trip in 310us) vs 8TB/s HBM peak. 2x of FLA at B=128 with fp32 T=1 semantics = 10TB/s > peak => PHYSICALLY IMPOSSIBLE. Paths to 2x: (a) small-B (dispatch-bound): fix dispatch (CUDA graph/direct launch) + kernel parity => 2x+ achievable; (b) large-B: bf16 state round-trip halves traffic (floor 0.16ms < 2x-target 0.158ms) but trades accuracy (blog hack-E analog; G5 gate would need explicit relaxation); (c) multi-token in-kernel T-loop amortizes state traffic 1/T (helps speculative-decode/prefill, not single-token serving).
